id_pocatello_area_bouldering.blurb: A scattering of small bouldering areas around Pocatello in southeast Idaho, each a short drive from town. Everything here is bouldering, and the grades cover a wide range: a big supply of easy V0 to V3 problems, a solid middle in the V4 to V7 band, and a handful of V8 to V10 lines for the strong. The stone is mostly basalt, with some conglomerate mixed in. Massacre Rocks is the largest piece, with house-sized basalt blocks and many smaller boulders, and The Tumbleweeds comes next, followed by the Redhill Trail and WaveWall. At Massacre Rocks, spring and fall are the best seasons, summer gets too hot, and a sunny winter day can work when there is no snow.

ca_berkeley.blurb: Urban bouldering spread across several small city parks in the Berkeley hills, above the East Bay. Bouldering makes up most of the climbing, with problems from V0 into the V12 and V13 range and a generous supply of moderates, plus a modest number of top-rope, trad and sport lines. Indian Rock is made up of rhyolite outcrops formed by volcanic activity; the rocks stress difficulty over height, ropes are rarely used, and crash pads are the norm. Its main area sits mostly in shade, elimination problems are common, and the scene turns social after work and on weekends. Mortar Rock, Grizzly Peak Boulders and Remillard Park are the other larger pockets.

nh_wm_franconia_notch.blurb: A mountain pass in New Hampshire's White Mountains reached from the interstate, holding both summer rock and winter ice. Trad is the largest share, mostly 5.7 to 5.11 with a tail of harder lines, alongside a fair number of sport routes, a pocket of boulders, and ice climbs mostly from WI3 to WI5. The big feature is Cannon Cliff, an exfoliating granite dome about a thousand feet high, the largest vertical face in the Northeast; it draws rock climbers in summer and ice and mixed climbers in winter. Echo Crag, Profile Cliff and Artist's Bluff offer shorter outings, and Hounds Hump Ridge adds more routes. Bouldering is scattered in its own pockets.

pa_safe_harbor_north.blurb: A string of walls beside the Susquehanna River in south-central Pennsylvania, strung along a former rail line and spaced fairly far apart. Sport climbing dominates, with a smaller number of trad lines and top-ropes, and the grades run from the mid 5.6 range to 5.12 with most routes in the 5.8 to 5.11 band and the heaviest concentration around 5.10. Compared with the neighbouring southern section, the walls here are steeper and more spread out, some routes want a longer rope, and the shade is better. Expect fingery face climbing on slippery rock that is often less than vertical. Cool-weather days suit it best. Larger walls include Chimney of Horror, Alpine Wall, Zero Wing and the International Area.

ok_se_oklahoma.blurb: Southeast Oklahoma climbing is mostly sandstone, and the rock is typically boulder height. Bouldering is the main event, with a big supply of V0 to V3 problems, a decent middle, and some lines in the V8 to V11 range. Roped climbing is a smaller share, concentrated in trad and top-rope routes at Robbers Cave State Park near Wilburton, in the wooded Sans Bois hills, mostly from 5.6 to around 5.10. McGee Creek, near Atoka, is the most boulder-heavy of the sub-areas and holds well over half of the region's climbs. Lake Atoka and Limestone Gap add a few more.

ca_emeralds_the.blurb: A crag complex in the I-80 corridor of the Tahoe area, near Bowman, at roughly 4,500 feet. Sport climbing leads the way and bolts provide the protection, since crack features are scarce. Routes run from the 5.8 range up to 5.13, with the bulk in the 5.10 and 5.11 bands. Bouldering is the second big draw, mostly V0 to V3 with a few harder problems, and there is a small amount of trad and top-roping. The Benches is the largest sub-area, followed by Emeralds Bouldering, with The Gorge and The Oasis smaller. Spring and fall are the best seasons because the elevation is low for Tahoe, winter is typically snowed in, and most walls face northwest, so summer mornings can be shaded.
